t: The word theocracy, “rule of God”, was coined by the Jewish historian Josephus in the 1st century CE for a people whose law came from God and was administered by priests.
Popes ruled the Papal States from 756 to 1870, Dalai Lamas governed Tibet from 1642 to 1959, and since 1979 Iran’s constitution has placed a senior Islamic jurist at the head of the state.
Scholars debate which states count as theocracies: many distinguish rule by clergy from divine kingship, from caliphates bound by religious law, and from states that only have an official religion.
dyk: In 1750 Marthanda Varma, king of Travancore in southern India, gave his kingdom to the god Padmanabha, a form of Vishnu; he and his successors then ruled as the deity’s servants, with the title Padmanabhadasa.
ev: The rebuilt Temple in Jerusalem is dedicated; a priest-led Judean community forms around it under Persian rule
In Against Apion the Jewish historian Josephus coins “theocracy” for a constitution that gave all sovereignty to God
Pepin the Short grants the pope former Byzantine lands in Italy, founding the Papal States
Güshi Khan confers authority over Tibet on the Fifth Dalai Lama, founding the Ganden Phodrang government
Italian troops take Rome on 20 September, ending the Papal States
The Lateran Treaty creates Vatican City, where the pope holds all legislative, executive and judicial power
After the Tibetan uprising the 14th Dalai Lama flees to India, and the Lhasa government is dissolved
A revolution and a new constitution make Iran an Islamic Republic headed by a senior Shia jurist

f.power: A religious authority, whether a priesthood, a supreme cleric or a ruler held to be divinely guided, with the final say over law and government
f.legitimacy: The claim that sovereignty belongs to God or the gods, whose will is known through scripture, revelation, sacred law or an inspired leader
f.chosen: Usually by religious bodies rather than voters: popes are elected by cardinals, Dalai Lamas are found as reincarnations, and Iran’s Supreme Leader is chosen by an assembly of jurists
f.examples: Judea under the high priests, the Papal States, Tibet under the Ganden Phodrang, the Prince-Bishopric of Montenegro, the Islamic Republic of Iran, Vatican City
